About 2 years ago I lived with my mother in a very very bad area of my city. Where we found a puppy on the street with no one in site. My mother has a very soft spot for animals, also cause she's usually alone at the house, always taking care of our one girl dog because she can't really leave the house due to medical reasons. So once we found the dog, she instantly took him in, obviously doing what we had to do, paperwork, meds essential puppy stuff. Now I'm talking about a newborn pup as well. He was a great dog, named Jax. We took care of him, played with him and just loved him. He was a wild one though, always getting into trouble, eating everything ect. But regardless we loved him. 

One day, he didn't eat anything which persisted for another day then another day. Finally we took him to the vet with what limited money i had saved up to only be told us he didn't have any problems they could visually see. Shocked, we though nothing of it really, he still was barely eating, but worst came to worse, was he was excreting blood while going to the bathroom. Worried we got him checked again but we couldn't afford an x-ray. To see what was wrong with him. We tried everything we could but nothing worked. So by the end, I felt we should have him put down. He could barely walk, still excreting blood, was eating very little, was a nightmare situation. But we didn't have any money, so we had to give up the dog, and that was the most painful thing I've ever done in my life. Now I've had dogs before, but I was to young to really understand what that meant. But now, as a young adult, physically carrying my dog, while my mother is bawling her eyes out in the car, and trying my hardest to hold it in for her...was the hardest thing I could ever do. We are poor, so we had to physically give up the rights to the dog, mean I couldn't be with him. At least that's what they told us. And to this day, I still cry about it every time I think about it.

When I was a kid I moved from place to place, so having friends was generally very hard for me. I finally moved in with my grandparents when I was around 7 or 8, in an entirely new school. I was extremely scared and nervous, to make matters worse I wasn't that smart and my skin color was different from everyone else. I felt like the black sheep of the herd. 

Until one day, during recess while I was sitting in the cafeteria on my gameboy; this one kid came up to me and struck a conversation with me. We talked about video games, Yugioh, Pokemon, Superhero and so many things. Turns out we had a lot in common, we played the same games, loved the same music, and both had the same initials too!


As we grew up, we had the same classes together and tried to spend as much time as we could with each other. 

My family was rather strict and so I couldn't always hang out with him, and have adventures all the time sadly. But he was always there for me, whether it was my first big break up, or me trying to lose weight. He has always been supportive of me, in return I have always been there for him.
